subject: Re: Sedgewick on-prem egress packet fragmentation + SNAT port collisions
messages:

Cc: netops@sedgewick-med.com, jill.park@sedgewick-med.com

Subject: Intermittent large-packet failures to Redwood private pool

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing intermittent failures from our on-prem Egress to the Redwood private pool this morning during a bulk data push. Files are timing out and some connections reset when payload sizes exceed ~1400 bytes. Flows to other SaaS endpoints are fine.

Attached is a quick traceroute and a packet capture from one upload (sedgewick_traceroute_20261005.txt, tcpdump excerpt). We also noticed connection resets correlate with high SNAT usage on our firewall.

Can Redwood ops confirm if we're hitting any port exhaustion on the SNAT gateway or if there's fragmentation happening mid-path? This is impacting our nightly syncs.

Thanks,
Tom
--
Tom Ellis
IT Infrastructure Manager | Sedgewick Medical

Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet failures to Redwood private pool

Tom — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We're opening an internal triage. Briefly:

- We'll validate SNAT table usage on our private egress nodes and check for ephemeral port collisions.
- We'll run controlled uploads from your CIDRs to reproduce MTU/fragmentation behavior and correlate with our kernel logs.
- Can you confirm whether your firewall is doing MSS clamping or GSO/GRO offload? Also send a short list of the client source IP ranges used for the bulk push.

I'm looping in Stephanie (networks) and Vivek (oncall infra) who will take point on traces and playbook remediation. We'll update within 4 hours with initial findings and an interim mitigation.

—Aditya

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@sedgewick-med.com>, NetOps Sedgewick <netops@sedgewick-med.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Sedgewick egress - first-pass traces attached

Team — internal notes and artifacts from customer (see attachments). Repro steps I ran from our staging nodes against a Sedgewick test endpoint:

1) Replayed a 16KB upload with standard socket MTU; observed fragmentation after our last hop to their firewall.
2) Kernel dmesg on our egress node showed: "TCP: possible SYN/ACK bug? conntrack: table full?" ~ not definitive.
3) Ephemeral port usage during the replay peaked at ~61k active mappings on their SNAT pool (customer reported similar).

Initial hypothesis: asymmetric MTU handling combined with SNAT ephemeral port collisions causing mid-flow resets. Two likely contributory items: (A) customer's firewall is not doing MSS clamping (so fragments are sent but downstream path or our security group drops oversized fragments), (B) our SNAT pool has tighter ephemeral mapping timeouts causing reuse during bursts.

Immediate asks for Steph/Vivek:
- Steph: can you check per-node iptables/conntrack stats and confirm conntrack table utilization across the private egress cluster? Also validate whether our LB is setting DF flag or accidentally rewriting DF.
- Vivek: please pull kernel tcp_offload/GRO/GSO settings and check if we have any mtu clamping on the interface to their VPC peer.

I'll provide the repro capture and a suggested playbook patch (proposed_playbook_patch.diff) that ramps conntrack max and enables conservative SNAT port allocation as temporary mitigation.

-Aditya
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@sedgewick-med.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Sedgewick egress - first-pass traces attached

Adding my findings from today's triage run (summary):

- Conntrack: per-node conntrack usage was ~78% on the primary egress node during replay (table size = 262144). Some entries were in TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT; timeouts were standard. Bumping nf_conntrack_max to 393216 brought usage down to ~45% under the same load.
- SNAT ports: observed increased port churn and occasional port reuse when ephemeral allocation hit ~61k. The kernel /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range is default (32768 - 60999) — which explains collisions under very high concurrency. Expanding to 1024 - 65535 reduced collision rate in test.
- MTU/fragmentation: our interface to the customer's VPC peer had no explicit MTU clamp. I reproduced fragmentation when sending 1500-byte payloads with DF cleared; however, packets with DF=1 fail if path MTU below 1500. Their firewall (from customer's pcap) is dropping fragments with overlapping offsets — looks like a reassembly limit set low on their device.

Actionable remediation (recommended order):
1) Temporary: expand ip_local_port_range to 1024-65535 on the egress nodes and bump nf_conntrack_max — apply as hotfix to target nodes serving Sedgewick.
2) Near-term: enable conservative SNAT port allocation and increase conntrack garbage-collection thresholds (patch attached).
3) Coordination ask for customer: ask their NetOps to enable MSS clamping on the firewall towards Redwood peer and raise IP reassembly buffers; also confirm no packet-normalizer is dropping fragments.
4) Longer-term: add per-tenant SNAT pools to isolate high-churn accounts.

I'll prepare the playbook PR and can push hotfix to a controlled canary group. Recommend scheduling a short joint window tonight 22:00-23:00 PT for hotfix and post-check.

—Vivek
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Action plan: hotfix window + coordination (Sedgewick)

Tom / NetOps team — quick update and plan based on triage:

Summary: we found two orthogonal contributors: (1) your firewall drops / fails on fragmented packets (reassembly limit / normalization), and (2) our ephemeral port range was hitting the upper bound causing reuse under burst, which increases TCP reset probability during re-transmit/reassembly.

Planned steps (tonight, 22:00-23:00 PT):
- Redwood will apply hotfix to canary egress nodes serving Sedgewick: expand ip_local_port_range, bump nf_conntrack_max, and enable conservative SNAT allocation. (Attachment: proposed_playbook_patch.diff)
- Sedgewick NetOps: please enable MSS clamping on outbound policy toward Redwood peer and increase IP reassembly buffers if possible. If you prefer, we can apply the hotfix to a small subset and wait for your firewall change before broad rollout.
- Verification: after canary hotfix, we'll run three controlled 16KB uploads and share tcpdump/traceroute for correlation.

If you approve the joint window, we will proceed and post a full rollback playbook in case of regressions.

Approve?

Thanks,
